The same people who INVENTED the climate hoaxes and the COVID scam are telling us to SLOW DOWN our AI capabilities.

Democrats want China to win the AI race. Not on our watch.

Whoever wins AI, wins. https://t.co/o4NMuxNgq6

deepseek.reason: The speaker says Democrats want China to win the AI race and declares 'Not on our watch,' endorsing competition priority.
deepseek.confidence_reason: The statement explicitly frames China as the race opponent and rejects letting China win.

china_race_dynamics.text: Agreed! WE MUST WIN THE AI RACE!!! 🇺🇸 @RichardGrenell https://t.co/tqDvaG6juC

deepseek.reason: The speaker explicitly says 'WE MUST WIN THE AI RACE,' endorsing competition with China as a priority.
deepseek.confidence_reason: The statement directly and unambiguously endorses winning the AI race.

china_race_dynamics.text: So if Congress acts, it will tend to overreact and stifle innovation. And everybody needs to understand there's a race to quantum computing. [...] And China is trying to use AI to beat us in the quantum race, and if they get there first, it is a winner-take-all race. This is the nuclear race all over again, and the stakes are higher. We must win this, and we must not stifle innovation.

deepseek.reason: The speaker calls the China AI/quantum race winner-take-all and says 'We must win this,' endorsing competition priority.
deepseek.confidence_reason: The statement explicitly frames China as a race competitor and calls for winning, though it also discusses innovation concerns.

china_race_dynamics.text:
America’s AI industry MUST coordinate with American cybersecurity partners to ensure our models and capabilities are not sabotaged by foreign actors.

If Chinese AI capabilities surpass ours, we become beholden to them. https://t.co/Jc54Mtvd9j

deepseek.reason: The speaker warns that Chinese AI surpassing the US would make America beholden, endorsing China competition as a priority.

china_race_dynamics.text:
🚨China is stealing American AI models and jailbreaking them to attack, censor, and sabotage us. 

American AI dominance is essential to preserve our free and safe society. https://t.co/rxNFwsmHUD

deepseek.reason: The speaker warns about China stealing and weaponizing American AI and says American AI dominance is essential, endorsing competition with China as a priority.
deepseek.confidence_reason: The statement explicitly names China and frames American AI dominance as essential against Chinese actions.

china_race_dynamics.text: Here is what concerns me. When the cheap, capable, easy option for an AI model is Chinese, the rest of the world will build on it. [...] We cannot let the world grow dependent on Chinese AI the way it grew dependent on other Chinese technologies we are now scrambling to address.

deepseek.reason: The speaker warns that the world will build on cheap Chinese AI and says the US cannot let the world become dependent on Chinese AI, endorsing competition with China as a priority.
deepseek.confidence_reason: The concern about global dependence on Chinese AI implies a clear competitive priority, though no specific policy tool is named.

china_race_dynamics.text: There is an AI arms race. Jailbroken AI used by our adversaries poses a monumental cyber threat. As Cyber Chairman, I am doing everything I can to stop it. https://t.co/EPzN7HShbJ

deepseek.reason: The statement refers generally to an AI arms race and unspecified adversaries, without identifying China or addressing competition with China specifically.
deepseek.confidence_reason: China is not named and 'adversaries' is too vague to tie this statement to the China race dynamics target.

astra.reason: The speaker discusses an AI arms race and unnamed adversaries without identifying China.
astra.confidence_reason: Connecting the unnamed adversaries to China would require evidence outside the statement.

china_race_dynamics.text: I mean, I see a horizon that we can't quite define because of the rapidness and just the evolving nature of the technology. I go back to kind-of the arms race. There was a point at which, between the United States and Russia, there was this detente, there was this, you know, mutually-assured destruction, where it was at some point we all had enough nukes to kill everybody and blow the whole world up. It was all about delivery systems at that point. AI is different. There is no horizon. There is no kind-of point at which I think it stops, that there is a ceiling.
china_race_dynamics.context: House committee hearing on quantum, AI, and cloud cybersecurity; Rep. Ogles questions a witness from Anthropic during the five-minute member questioning period.

deepseek.reason: The statement discusses a general AI arms race without mentioning China or a China competition priority.
deepseek.confidence_reason: No China reference or China AI competition stance appears in the statement.

China is trying to create artificial hackers with OUR AI. We must win.

No Committee in the House wants to touch this AI issue because it will put a large target on members ’ backs. Having this hearing will put my staff, my family, and every committee member at risk from foreign data hackers. We accept the risk. We will be bold. 

Now that I am Cyber Chairman, I am making this my battle. I will fight the culture war, and now I vow to lead the cyber war. Stay tuned.
